title: Nasruddin and the Beggar

full_text:
A beggar knocked at Nasruddin's street door. Nasruddin, who was resting in his second-story study, leaned out: "What do you want?"

"Come down, master, I have an urgent matter!" called the beggar.

Nasruddin climbed all the way down the long flight of stairs to the door. "What is it?"

"Give me a copper coin for bread," whispered the beggar.

Nasruddin looked at him: "Follow me upstairs." The beggar climbed the stairs with high hopes. In the study, Nasruddin turned to him: "I have no money for you."

"Why didn't you tell me that downstairs?" complained the beggar.

"Why did you call me all the way downstairs merely to ask for money?" replied Nasruddin.
moral: Do not demand that others climb mountains merely to hear a refusal.

Acting in hasty anger without listening

By shouting loudly and blaming friends

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach readers?
options: Patience, honesty, and humility lead to lasting harmony
quiz.hint: Think about how justice and truth prevail.
